description:
`.github/workflows/auto-merge-on-open.yml` (lines 31-48: the checkout, base-branch
fetch, and "Check soundness-critical paths" step) checks out the PR at its own
HEAD and then runs `_project/scripts/auto_merge_soundness_paths.py` *from that
same checkout*. For a same-repo (non-fork) PR — the normal case for this
single-maintainer-owned repo where contributors push branches directly — the
script executing the predicate is whatever version the PR itself introduces. A
PR that edits `auto_merge_soundness_paths.py` (e.g. narrows `SOUNDNESS_PREFIXES`,
or the workflow file itself) evaluates its own diff against its own modified
rules, so it can neutralize its review gate in the same commit that would
otherwise have triggered it.

Note honestly: with the repo-layer ruleset review requirement from
auto-merge-review-gate-admin-enforcement enforced (once its deferred admin
action lands), this workflow's withholding behavior is defense-in-depth, not
the primary control — the ruleset's `pull_request` rule would block a
zero-approval squash-merge regardless of what this workflow decides. This item
is still worth doing because (a) the ruleset enforcement is not yet live, and
(b) even once it is, a same-commit self-neutralization that quietly avoids
ever showing "review required" is a bad signal for reviewers relying on the
auto-merge state as a triage cue.

anti_patterns.dont: fork auto_merge_soundness_paths.py's logic into the workflow YAML as inline shell/python
anti_patterns.why: keep executing the actual script file (from the base ref) so there is exactly one implementation to maintain.

anti_patterns.dont: skip the base-branch fetch step's existing --no-tags behavior or change its shallow/full-history semantics; only add the base-ref file materialization after it.
treat this as a substitute for the ruleset-layer review requirement
anti_patterns.why: this is documented as defense-in-depth in the description; don't let this item's success_metrics imply it replaces auto-merge-review-gate-admin-enforcement.

preserves.behavior: The synchronize-event re-evaluation behavior (a later push that newly touches a soundness path flips auto-merge back off) continues to work.
The workflow's output contract (steps.soundness.outputs.soundness_path, consumed by the existing enable/disable auto-merge steps) is unchanged.
make pr-open's local invocation of the predicate is unaffected by this item (base-ref execution is CI-workflow-specific; a local developer already has full repo access).

prior_art.concept: .github/workflows/auto-merge-on-open.yml:31-48 — the checkout + soundness-check step being hardened; keep its step names and output contract (steps.soundness.outputs.soundness_path) stable so the enable/disable steps below it don't need changes.

Makefile:pr-open (~line 1163) — also invokes the predicate via `uv run --project _project/scripts`; out of scope for this item's local-CLI flow (a developer running make pr-open locally already has arbitrary code execution), but keep the two invocations' semantics compatible.
_project/scripts/auto_merge_soundness_paths.py — the predicate being protected; do not fork or duplicate its logic, only change which copy of the file gets executed.

verifications.description: Backstop workflow tests still pass with the added base-ref and self-touch assertions
verifications.expected: all tests pass, including the extended test_backstop_workflow_uses_shared_predicate_and_skips_auto_merge

verifications.command: gh run view <run-id> --log | grep -A3 'Check soundness-critical paths'
verifications.description: A workflow_dispatch or manual trace confirms /tmp/predicate.py is materialized from origin/develop, not the PR's HEAD copy, before the predicate runs
verifications.expected: log shows the git show origin/${{ github.base_ref }} step succeeding before the predicate invocation

work_units.notes:
In the "Check soundness-critical paths" step, before running the predicate,
materialize the base-ref version: `git show
"origin/${{ github.base_ref }}:_project/scripts/auto_merge_soundness_paths.py"
> /tmp/predicate.py` (base branch is already fetched by the preceding
"Fetch base branch" step), then invoke `python /tmp/predicate.py --stdin
--format github-output` instead of the checked-out repo path. Confirm the
script has no relative imports or sibling-file dependencies that would
break when run standalone from /tmp (check the top of
auto_merge_soundness_paths.py — it currently has none, keep it that way or
copy siblings too if that changes).
work_units.summary: Fetch and execute the base-ref copy of the predicate script instead of the PR's own checkout copy

work_units.notes:
Add an explicit check: if the PR's diff touches
_project/scripts/auto_merge_soundness_paths.py or
.github/workflows/auto-merge-on-open.yml, force soundness_path=true
regardless of what the base-ref predicate returns for the rest of the
diff. This closes the residual gap where a PR could still edit the
predicate to make future PRs unsafe, without itself needing owner review
under the base-ref-only check (base-ref execution alone stops the
predicate from judging its own diff leniently, but does not by itself
flag "this diff touches the predicate" as inherently review-worthy).
work_units.summary: Treat modification of the predicate or the workflow itself as soundness=true

work_units.notes:
Extend tests/unit/test_auto_merge_soundness_paths.py's
test_backstop_workflow_uses_shared_predicate_and_skips_auto_merge (which
currently string-matches the workflow YAML) with assertions for the new
`git show origin/.../auto_merge_soundness_paths.py` line and the
predicate/workflow self-touch check, so a future edit that removes the
base-ref execution regresses a fast unit test rather than only being
caught by manual review.
work_units.summary: Update or add a workflow-level test exercising the base-ref execution path
